newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher on soft U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher on soft U.S. data.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher again Friday, after another session aided by gains in U.S. Treasuries after soft economic data.
Traders said a fall in U.S. producer prices of 0.3 percent further reduced chances of higher U.S. interest rates in July.
Still, with the amount of recent spread tightening "there could be some profit-taking," said one trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 94-3/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.05 at 121.15.
Despite the feeling that record low spreads makes the market appear expensive, traders said Argentina's strong economic fundamentals justify further gains.
Next week's auctions of treasury bills and treasury bonds will be a gauge of whether there is still strong demand for Argentine debt instruments, said players.
"I think demand at the auctions will be strong," said another trader.
The local market is shut Monday for Flag Day.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.45 percent from 5.50 percent.
